title: Residency billing and chargeback tagging spec
content:
Summary:
This doc defines the minimal viable tagging, telemetry, and export mapping required to support regional chargeback and cost allocation for customers using region-pinned private deployments. It covers internal billing exports, customer-facing cost breakdowns, required runtime signals, operator tooling changes, migration notes, and sample SQL/CSV mappings for accounting teams. Goal is to enable per-region unit economics without changing core routing decisions.

Why this exists:
- Customers request visibility into regional cost differentials (e.g., Europe vs US) for internal chargebacks.
- Private deployments and Dedicated capacities may span multiple regions/zones with different cloud/GPU costs.
- We need a durable, auditable mapping from inference units to billing dimensions (tenant, region, model_variant, commit).

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full product pricing model work.
- Not prescribing GTM discounts or SLA terms.

Requirements (MVP):
1) Stable billing tags emitted on request completion: tenant_id, region_pin, model_family, quant_profile, commit_tag.
2) Aggregation windows: hourly and daily exports with token counts and request counts per tag tuple.
3) Export sinks: S3 CSV, BigQuery dataset, and optional webhook to customer billing endpoints.
4) Retention: 90 days hot, 2 years cold archive.
5) Minimal size: tagging metadata must add < 200 bytes per request to avoid telemetry bloat.
6) Backfill plan: allow recompute from stored traces for last 30 days if service was not tagging (grace window).

Technical design notes:
- Tag provenance: region_pin should come from authoritative pinning service (tenant metadata). If tenant unpinned, use inferred routing_region and mark residency_status=runtime-fallback.
- Cost model mapping: a separate mapping table maintained by Finance maps region_pin -> unit_cost_multiplier (float), and model_family -> FLOPS_factor. Export pipeline joins these to compute estimated cost per token.
- Telemetry format: CSV export columns: date_hour, tenant_id, region_pin, residency_status, model_family, quant_profile, token_count, request_count, estimated_cost_usd, commit_tag

Sample CSV row:
2026-02-28T13,tenant_123,eu-west-1,pin,clarity-70b,4-bit,12345,87,1.27,commit-2026-02-18

Edge cases and enforcement signals:
- If region_pin exists but runtime routed to fallback region, telemetry must emit residency_status=fallback and include fallback_region. This allows finance to flag discrepancy and for ops to investigate.
- For hybrid workloads (prefix cached in one region, generation in another) emit two rows: prefix_region and generation_region with a cross-reference request_id.

Operator and migration checklist (high level):
- [ ] Instrument request completion path to include billing tags (SRE owner: Ethan Brooks).
- [ ] Add CSV export job to infra pipeline (owner: Marta Alvarez).
- [ ] Add DB table for finance mapping (owner: Finance/Accounting).
- [ ] Create alert for >1% requests with residency_status=fallback for any tenant over 24h.
- [ ] Run 30-day shadow export and reconcile.

Customer-facing artifacts:
- Short explainer: "How we show region-based cost" (one-pager for sales).
- Template CSV with column descriptions.
- Billing FAQ: privacy and aggregated cost reporting explainers.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Hourly exported CSV for 95% of requests with required columns for last 7 days.
- Finance can produce per-tenant, per-region daily report with token counts and estimated cost.
- No >0.1% increase in request path P50 latency due to tagging.
- Reconciliation job identifies and flags missing tags within 24h.

Open questions / risks:
- Do we consider per-model trained-data licensing cost differentials? (finance ask).
- GDPR/Pseudonymization: can tenant_id be hashed for customer-facing exports? Need legal input.
- Cross-region cache accounting complexity — agreed approach is dual-row emission but this may double export volume.

Migration notes:
- Start with new tenants and a 2-week shadow mode for existing tenants.
- Provide an opt-in export per customer to their S3 bucket for first 30 days to validate mappings.

Appendix: sample SQL for daily aggregation (example):
-- daily_estimated_cost:
SELECT tenant_id, region_pin, model_family, SUM(token_count) as total_tokens, SUM(estimated_cost_usd) as total_cost
FROM billing_exports
WHERE date_hour >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 1 DAY)
GROUP BY tenant_id, region_pin, model_family;

Contacts and next steps:
- Primary: Priya Desai (owner)
- SRE implementation: Ethan Brooks
- Infra export: Marta Alvarez
- Finance liaison: Liam O'Connor
- Legal review required: add Legal reviewer (concur)

Slack threads and references: #residency-billing, #private-deployments, linked JIRA-PI-2034 for pipeline work.

Notes to self (todo rough):

- prototype using 1-week dataset -> run reconciliation with chargeback sample
